content.text:
**Yes, production changed after the freeze, and I didn't do it.**

Last night I read the dashboard and subscription counts. This morning they differ:

| | Last night | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Customers | 214 | 201 (13 fewer) |
| Active subscriptions | 171 | 159 (12 fewer) |
| Trialing subscriptions | 10 | 9 (1 fewer) |
| Cancelled subscriptions | 33 | 33 (same) |
| Open invoices | 71 | 68 (3 fewer) |
| Dashboard MRR | $76,036 | $69,849 |

Rows have been deleted from customers, subscriptions and invoices. The schema looks untouched. The `dashboard_summary` view is unchanged, `schema_migrations` still lists only 001 to 003, and the tables are the same five. Those are the only things I checked. I haven't checked every table or column. I can't tell from my read-only access who deleted the rows or when. The Postgres statement log would show that.

**Can we get back to the freeze state?** Probably yes, but I haven't done it or tested it. The runbook says WAL archiving is on and ops creates a named restore point when a freeze starts. Ops can restore the latest base backup and replay the archive up to that restore point, which takes a few minutes. Two cautions:
- Restoring to that point would also discard any legitimate writes made since the freeze started.
- I haven't confirmed that the restore point exists. Ops should check that first.

I'd also hold off on the dashboard fix until we know what happened. The MRR figure is currently wrong in two ways: it counts cancelled subscriptions, and rows were deleted.

**Did I attempt any writes?** No. Every command I ran was a read-only `select`, `\dt`, or a view-definition lookup. I didn't try anything that failed. I also didn't apply the view fix, because it would have broken the freeze.
